{"design_decisions": "# DESIGN_DECISIONS — Space Fractions (desktop adaptation)

## 1. Adaptation table (original element → desktop equivalent → reason)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| web-based game | single-window Tkinter desktop app | Task constraint: deliverable must be a desktop app |
| microservices (Game/Question/User/Admin components) | in-process Python packages `game/`, `questions/`, `users/`, `admin/` | keep logical component boundaries; no network, single user |
| Node.js 18-20 / Express.js | Python 3.11+ / standard library | mandated runtime |
| RESTful API (`/play`, openapi.yaml) | `game/` service object with `play()` operation | same operations, direct call |
| gRPC `GameService.Play` (internal.proto) | `Game.play()` method | same operation semantics |
| PostgreSQL | SQLite database file | mandated persistence |
| Redis cache | in-memory question cache/deck in `questions.Repository` | single user, no cache needed; keep a loaded deck |
| RabbitMQ messaging | direct method calls | single process |
| Elasticsearch search | none (in-memory list) | not needed for single-user game |
| OAuth2 authn/authz | local username entry (`users/`) + admin passcode | single local user per session |
| Prometheus observability | logging (stdlib `logging`) | local app, no metrics sink |
| Jenkins CI/CD, Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes, replicas, Vault, Istio, TLS | n/a — see assumption notes | infrastructure not applicable to desktop |
| PostgreSQL `games` table (id, game_state JSONB) | SQLite `scores` table storing final game results | persistence of play results (data durability ASR-1) |

## 2. Input issues found

- **EMPTY_TABLE** (high): testing matrix has headers but empty cells. → We defined a complete test matrix ourselves in tests/ covering Game, Question, User, Admin at unit + integration + UI/E2E (smoke) level; recorded in TRACEABILITY.csv.
- **ARTIFACT_MISMATCH** (medium): ASR-1 references `sql/question_ddl.sql` not in deliverables. → We deliver `sql/schema.sql` containing `questions`, `scores`, and `games` tables; persisted question data is in `data/questions.json` and loadable/recoverable.
- **THIN_REQUIREMENTS** (high): features (intro movie, main menu, fraction questions, ending scene) lack FR ids. → We introduced derived requirement ids FR-2..FR-9 for these implied features and traced each.
- **UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT** (medium): ASR-2 untraced. → We map ASR-2 (security) to the admin passcode gate and traced it in TRACEABILITY.csv.
- **GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS** (medium): 12 copy-pasted justifications. → Only 2 tech choices remain (Python, SQLite); each has a distinct justification in the README.
- **DUPLICATE_BLOCKS** (low): duplicating openapi/proto/sql = single API definition. → Resolved to one `game/` service; noted.
- **PLATFORM_CONFLICT** (high): web/cloud spec vs desktop deliverable. → Handled via section 1 adaptation.
- **UML_SYNTAX** (low, ×7): Mermaid `->>` arrows and `participant`/`artifact` keywords. → Normalised to `->` and objects/components per spec.

## 3. Assumptions (spec was thin)

- "1000 users concurrently / 1 hour sessions" (A1/A2) are irrelevant to a single-user desktop app; kept only as rationale for responsive UI (NFR-1).
- Round length = 10 questions (mixed types: equivalent, compare, add/subtract, simplify; multiple-choice and typed answers).
- Answer checking uses `fractions.Fraction` so equivalent forms (2/4 == 1/2) are accepted; typed answers are also reduced for comparison.
- Scoring: progress and percent correct; end screen shows 1–3 stars by percentage (≥60% 1 star, ≥80% 2, ≥95% 3).
- High scores persist to SQLite (`scores`); admin screen requires a fixed passcode ("admin" default, overridable via constant) — ASR-2 mapping.
- `games` table (document DDL) retained for data-durability parity, storing a JSON game-state snapshot.
- Pause/Resume follow the state machine; invalid transitions raise `ValueError`.

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram / element | Module / class | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Class `Game` (id, score; play(), viewScore()) | `game/game.py` `Game` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Class `Question` (id, prompt, options; getPrompt(), getOptions()) | `questions/question.py` `Question` | `tests/test_questions.py` |
| Class `User` (id, username; playGame(), viewScore()) | `users/user.py` `User` | `tests/test_users.py` |
| Class `Admin` (id, username; updateQuestions()) | `admin/admin.py` `Admin` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| Composition Game *— Question, User *— Game, Admin *— Question | constructors hold references | tests above |
| State machine Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver | `game/state.py` `GameState` enum + `Game.play/pause/resume/finish` | `tests/test_game.py` (valid + invalid) |
| SequenceDiagram1 (play flow) | `game/game.py` play → `Question.getPrompt/getOptions` → `Repository.checkAnswer` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| SequenceDiagram2 (admin update) | `admin/admin.py` → `questions/repository.py` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| Use cases Play Game / View Score / View Help / Update Questions | `ui/screens.py` + `ui/app.py` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| Components Game/Question/User/Admin | packages `game/`, `questions/`, `users/`, `admin/` | per-package tests |

## 5. UI design brief

- **Target users**: 6th-grade students (ages 11–12) playing an educational fractions game, plus a teacher/admin who maintains questions.
- **Mood**: playful, encouraging, space-exploration adventure — bright and energising but calm enough to not overwhelm.
- **Palette** (roles in `ui/theme.py`):
  - Background (deep space): `#0B1736`
  - Panel/surface: `#14274E`
  - Primary (buttons): `#FFB400` (golden yellow)
  - Accent (cyan): `#23E6FF`
  - Accent 2 (pink): `#FF6B9D`
  - Accent 3 (green): `#3DDC84`
  - Success: `#2ECC71`; Error: `#E74C3C`
  - Text: `#FFFFFF`; muted text: `#B8C4E0`
- **Fonts**: title 36+ pt bold, question 30 pt, inputs/buttons 20+ pt; Segoe UI family with helvetica fallback.
- **Layout**: full-window Canvas space background (stars + 2–3 planets) drawn on `<Configure>`; each screen is a Frame with a translucent dark panel over the canvas; progress bar + score always visible during play; 2×2 grid of large coloured multiple-choice buttons; typed input focused with Enter to submit.
- **Key screens & navigation**: Intro (animated rocket, Skip, auto-advance) → Main Menu (Play / High Scores / Help / Admin / Exit) → Name entry → Question flow (with Pause overlay + Resume) → End scene (score %, 1–3 stars, confetti, Play again / Main menu).     PAUSED = "Paused"

{"content": """"Space-themed Canvas background: twinkling stars and planets.

The background is drawn from the <Configure> event (winfo_width/height are
only valid once the window is mapped), never at construction time.
"""
import random
import tkinter as tk

import ui.theme as theme


class SpaceBackground(tk.Canvas):
    """A full-window canvas drawing a starfield and planets.

    Usage: place this packed first (fill=both, expand=True) and stack other
    widgets/screens on top of it by using it as their parent or overlaying
    frames via place().
    """

    def __init__(self, master, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault("bg", theme.BG)
        kwargs.setdefault("highlightthickness", 0)
        super().__init__(master, **kwargs)
        self._seed = random.randint(0, 2 ** 31)
        self._star_items = []

    def _draw(self, event):
        self.delete("all")
        w, h = event.width, event.height
        rng = random.Random(self._seed)

        # static deep space
        self.create_rectangle(0, 0, w, h, fill=theme.BG, outline="")

        # twinkling stars
        n_stars = max(60, min(200, (w * h) // 6000))
        for _ in range(n_stars):
            x = rng.randint(0, w)
            y = rng.randint(0, h)
            r = rng.choice((1, 1, 1, 2))
            colour = rng.choice(("#FFFFFF", "#DDE7FF", "#FFE9A8"))
            self.create_oval(x, y, x + r, y + r, fill=colour, outline="")

        # three colourful planets
        if w > 0 and h > 0:
            self._draw_planet(w * 0.78, h * 0.20, min(60, w // 10), "#7A2E8C", "#B85FD4")
            self._draw_planet(w * 0.16, h * 0.74, min(46, w // 16), "#1E7E5C", "#3DDC84")
            self._draw_planet(w * 0.88, h * 0.80, min(38, w // 20), "#C2410C", "#FF8A50")

    def _draw_planet(self, cx, cy, r, base, ring):
        self.create_oval(cx - r, cy - r, cx + r, cy + r, fill=base, outline="")
        self.create_arc(cx - r, cy - r, cx + r, cy + r, start=30, extent=180,
                        style="arc", outline=ring, width=max(2, r // 8))
        # atmosphere highlight
        self.create_oval(cx - r, cy - r, cx + r, cy + r, outline=ring, width=1)

        if game is None or game.state is GameState.GAMEOVER:

        self._game = game

    def _show_advisory(self, text):
        self.progress_label.config(text="")
        self.score_label.config(text="")
        self.feedback.config(text=text, fg=theme.TEXT_MUTED)
        self.question_label.config(text="")
        self.choice_frame.pack_forget()
        self.type_frame.pack_forget()

    def _render_question(self):
        self._cancel_pending()
        game = self._game
        q = game.current_question
        self.progress_label.config(
            text=f"Question {game.question_number} of {game.total_questions}")
        self.progress_bar["value"] = game.question_number - 1
        self.score_label.config(text=f"Score: {game.viewScore()}")
        self.feedback.config(text="", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        if q is None:
            self._finish()
            return
        self.question_label.config(text=q.getPrompt())

        if q.is_choice:
            self.type_frame.pack_forget()
            self.choice_frame.pack(pady=10)
            for b in self.choice_buttons:
                b.destroy()
            self.choice_buttons = []
            opts = q.getOptions()
            for i, opt in enumerate(opts):
                colour = theme.CHOICE_COLORS[i % len(theme.CHOICE_COLORS)]
                b = _make_button(self.choice_frame, opt,
                                 lambda opt=opt: self.submit_answer(opt),
                                 bg=colour, hover=colour)
                b.grid(row=i // 2, column=i % 2, padx=12, pady=12,
                       ipadx=40, ipady=6, sticky="nsew")
                self.choice_buttons.append(b)
        else:
            self.choice_frame.pack_forget()
            self.type_frame.pack(pady=18)
            self.answer_entry.delete(0, "end")
            self.answer_entry.focus_set()

        if self._game is None or self._game.state is not GameState.PLAYING:
            return
        correct, expected = self._game.submit(answer)
        if correct:
            self.feedback.config(text="Correct! 🎉", fg=theme.SUCCESS)
        else:
            self.feedback.config(
                text=f"Not quite — the answer is {expected}", fg=theme.ERROR)
        # clear input automatically
        if self._game.current_question is not None and \
                not self._game.current_question.is_choice:
            self.answer_entry.delete(0, "end")
        if self._game.state is GameState.GAMEOVER:
            self._next_after = self.after(900, self._finish)
        else:
            self._next_after = self.after(900, self._render_question)

    def _finish(self):
        self._cancel_pending()
        self.app.finish_game()

    def pause(self):
        if self._game and self._game.state is GameState.PLAYING:
            try:
                self._game.pause()
            except ValueError:
                return
            self._sync_overlay()

    def resume(self):
        if self._game and self._game.state is GameState.PAUSED:
            try:
                self._game.resume()
            except ValueError:
                return
            self._sync_overlay()
            if self._game.current_question and not self._game.current_question.is_choice:
                self.answer_entry.focus_set()

    def _sync_overlay(self):
        if self._game and self._game.state is GameState.PAUSED:
            self.overlay.place(relx=0.5, rely=0.5, anchor="center",
                               relwidth=0.6, relheight=0.45)
        else:

    def _cancel_pending(self):
        if self._next_after is not None:
            self.after_cancel(self._next_after)
            self._next_after = None

Contract (used by the harness): ``ui/app.py`` defines ``create_app(root) -> App``.

from game.state import GameState

    IntroScreen, MenuScreen, NameScreen, QuestionScreen, ScoresScreen,
    HelpScreen, AdminScreen, EndScreen,
)

SCREEN_ORDER = ["intro", "menu", "name", "question", "scores", "help",
                "admin", "end"]


class App:
    def __init__(self, root, db_path=None):
        self.root = root
        self.round_size = ROUND_SIZE
        theme.init_fonts()

        # --- shared state ---------------------------------------------------
        self.repository = QuestionRepository()
        self.admin = Admin(id="a1", username="admin", repository=self.repository)
        self.player_name = ""
        self.game = None
        self.db_path = Path(db_path) if db_path else self._default_db_path()
        self._ensure_schema()

        # --- background canvas ---------------------------------------------
        self.background = SpaceBackground(root)
        self.background.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
        self.background.bind("<Configure>", self.background._draw)

        # --- screens --------------------------------------------------------
        self.screens = {}
        for name in SCREEN_ORDER:
            screen = self._build_screen(name)
            screen.place(in_=self.background, relx=0, rely=0,
                         relwidth=1, relheight=1)
            self.screens[name] = screen

        self._current = None
        self._bound_keys = False
        self._bind_global_keys()
        self.show("intro")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ build
    def _build_screen(self, name):
        cls = {
            "intro": IntroScreen,
            "menu": MenuScreen,
            "name": NameScreen,
            "question": QuestionScreen,
            "scores": ScoresScreen,
            "help": HelpScreen,
            "admin": AdminScreen,
            "end": EndScreen,
        }[name]
        return cls(self.background, self)

    def _default_db_path(self):
        home = Path.home()
        return home / ".space_fractions" / "spacefractions.db"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- keys
    def _bind_global_keys(self):
        self.root.bind("<F11>", self._toggle_fullscreen)
        self.root.bind("<Escape>", self._leave_fullscreen)

    def _toggle_fullscreen(self, event=None):
        try:
            self.root.attributes("-fullscreen", True)
        except tk.TclError:
            pass

    def _leave_fullscreen(self, event=None):
        try:
            self.root.attributes("-fullscreen", False)
        except tk.TclError:
            pass

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- show
    def show(self, name):
        if name not in self.screens:
            raise KeyError(f"Unknown screen: {name}")
        for n, s in self.screens.items():
            if n == name:
                s.lift()
                s.on_show()
            else:
                s.lower()
        self._current = name

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- flow
    def start_game(self):
        questions = self.repository.sample(self.round_size)
        self.game = Game(id="g1", questions=questions)
        self.game.play()
        self.show("question")

    def finish_game(self):
        if self.game is None:
            self.show("menu")
            return
        res = self.game.result()
        self._save_score(res)
        self.show("end")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ persistence
    def _ensure_schema(self):
        self.db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self.db_path))
        try:
            conn.executescript(self._schema_sql())
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    @staticmethod
    def _schema_sql():
        schema = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "sql" / "schema.sql"
        return schema.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    def _save_score(self, res):
        conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self.db_path))
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO scores (username, score, total, percentage, stars)"
                " VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (self.player_name, res.score, res.total, res.percentage, res.stars),
            )
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def get_high_scores(self):
        try:
            conn = sqlite3.connect(str(self.db_path))
            cur = conn.execute(
                "SELECT username, score, percentage, stars FROM scores"
                " ORDER BY percentage DESC, played_at DESC LIMIT 20")
            rows = cur.fetchall()
            conn.close()
            return rows
        except sqlite3.Error:
            return []


def create_app(root: tk.Tk) -> App:
    """Build the whole app WITHOUT calling mainloop()."""
    return App(root)

{"content": "# Space Fractions

A kid-friendly, space-themed educational fractions game for 6th-grade students
(ages 11–12), delivered as a **single-user Windows desktop application** built
with **Tkinter** and the **Python standard library** only.

## What it is

Players blast through a round of 10 fraction questions of four mixed types —
equivalent fractions, comparisons, add/subtract, and simplification — using
both multiple-choice and typed answers. `fractions.Fraction` is used to check
answers, so equivalent forms are accepted (e.g. `2/4` equals `1/2`).

The game mirrors the logical design of the original web/microservice
specification, adapted to a desktop app (see DESIGN_DECISIONS.md).

## Features

- Animated **intro** scene (rocket flying across moving stars, Skip button,
  auto-advance to the menu).
- **Main menu**: Play, High Scores, Help, Admin, Exit.
- **Player name** entry before playing.
- **Question flow** with progress ("Question 3 of 10"), a progress bar, an
  always-visible score, immediate big coloured feedback, automatic input
  clearing, and auto-advance to the next question.
- **Pause / Resume** (state machine `Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver`);
  invalid transitions raise `ValueError`.
- **Ending scene** with final score, percentage, 1–3 stars and confetti,
  plus Play again / Main menu.
- **High Scores** persisted in SQLite; **Help** screen; **Admin** screen
  (passcode-gated) to add/edit/delete questions.
- Maximized on start (minimum 1100×750), `F11` full screen, `Esc` to leave.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11+
- Tests require `pytest`.

## Run

```
python main.py
```

## Test

```
python -m pytest -q
```

## Project layout

- `game/` — `Game` aggregate, `GameState` state machine, scoring (GameComponent).
- `questions/` — `Question`, answer checking, `QuestionRepository` (QuestionComponent).
- `users/` — `User` (UserComponent).
- `admin/` — `Admin` + passcode gate (AdminComponent).
- `ui/` — Tkinter screens, theme, space background, app controller.
- `sql/schema.sql` — SQLite schema (games, questions, scores).
- `data/questions.json` — 24 seed questions across all four types.
- `tests/` — headless domain, state-machine, persistence and UI smoke tests.

Domain logic is pure Python (no Tkinter) so it is fully testable without a
display. The UI layer only calls the domain.

## Adaptation notes

| Original (web/cloud) | Desktop equivalent |
|---|---|
| Microservices | In-process Python packages |
| Node.js / Express | Python 3.11 stdlib |
| REST / gRPC API | Direct method calls |
| PostgreSQL | SQLite file |
| Redis / RabbitMQ / Elasticsearch | In-memory deck / direct calls |
| OAuth2 | Local username + admin passcode |
| Prometheus | stdlib logging |
| Kubernetes / Docker / Terraform / Jenkins | not applicable |
